newsitem.title: ARGENTINA: Argentine stocks end lower, seen slipping further.
newsitem.headline: Argentine stocks end lower, seen slipping further.

text.p: Argentine stocks pulled back Friday to close flat on the week, jolted by U.S. payrolls data, and dealers expected more losses early next week.

"The markets here, in the United States and Brazil were all taken by surprise by the numbers, and considering Wall Street had been rallying all week on other indicators the fall is logical," said Augusto Milou at brokers Galicia Valores.
The blue-chip MerVal index .MERV closed off 1.1 percent to 841.08, erasing the week's gains.
Milou predicted the MerVal might have to shed up to one or two percent more near-term before finding support.
"However, this fall is not being caused by sharp selling but rather by weaker demand, so you could call it a simple correction which is not really hurting the market," he added.
Floor volume shrank to 20.5 million pesos from 28.8 million Thursday and 32 million Wednesday, while over-the-counter turnover picked up to 96.9 million pesos from 92.5 million Thursday.

Traders were not overly concerned about the 4.8 percent dive in Brazil's Bovespa index .BVSP, saying it was unrelated to recent fears of a devaluation which caused a sharp correction on the bolsa in mid-July.
"Brazil was also hit by Wall Street, but there were other factors affecting it today like poor trade numbers and talk that several brokerages might be closed," another dealer said.
The Argentine broad market closed off 0.9 percent, with losers blasting winners 45 to nine and 15 issues closing flat.
The only main-tier risers were holding company Comercial del Plata and real estate developer Irsa, which advanced 1.2 percent and 0.5 percent, respectively.
Losers were led by carmaker Ciadea, down 6.0 percent, and construction firms Corcemar and Polledo, both off 3.0 percent.
